seed_intent: Per Shawn's live request, assess and prototype whether the 35 reasoning-strategy agents (plugins/pmcro-reasoning-strategy/agents/*.md) can be template-driven / declaratively generated, the same "declare once, generate projections" pattern already built this session for agent scaffolding (DECLARATIVE-GENERATIVE-AGENT-TEMPLATE.md + scaffold.py). Read chain-of-thought.md and self-refine.md in full this session: confirmed every strategy file shares near-identical frontmatter (laws and permissions are byte-identical across all 34 non-selector strategies; only family and reasoning.{logical_paradigms,operational_methods,domain_capabilities} vary) and an identical six-section body order (Purpose, When to Use, When Not to Use, Workflow, Validation, Output), with Output being fully mechanical per strategy id. This is a genuinely different rendering convention than AgentScaffoldSpec's SKILL.md/maf-inline targets (this is the single-file plugins/*/agents/*.md convention with id/package/kind/family/laws/permissions/reasoning frontmatter), so it needs its own small declarative spec + generator rather than overloading scaffold.py. Build a ReasoningStrategySpec schema + generator, prove it via round-trip on the two already-read strategies (chain-of-thought, self-refine): write a declarative spec for each, generate the .md, and diff against the real committed file to verify the generator reproduces (or intentionally, documented-ly, improves on) the real content - not fabricated confidence. Also separately note (but do not necessarily build this pass) that selector.md's Families-by-family list is mechanically derivable from the full spec set, while its Quick Selection Guide table is curated editorial content that isn't purely derivable and would need an explicit per-spec hint field if ever generated too.
